title: 'We Are Helpless'
text:
'We Are Helpless' is one of the newspaper articles in Red Dead Redemption 2.
TOWNS DECRY UNCHECKED VIOLENCE.
OUTLAW GANGS RUNNING RAMPANT.
LED BY NOTORIOUS CRIMINAL MICAH BELL.
A cacophony of outrage has been building at the lawlessness that prevails in towns across the area. Numerous outlaw gangs seem to operate unchecked or unstoppable by law enforcement, rendering terrified citizens helpless. The reward for the killing or capture of infamous outlaw Micah Bell and his gang was recently increased by government officials in response to the unanimous outcry from citizens that something must be done about this murderous gang of thieves and killers.
Mr. Bell and his associates continue their spree of killing and robbing while running roughshod over law enforcement. His acts of lawlessness rival that of Van der Linde himself. They pay no debts and dynamite banks and buildings as a recreational pastime. Bell has long been a suspect in the Blackwater Bank Robbery and Strawberry massacre back in 1899 and numerous train robberies that have ended in dismemberment or death of passengers in the years since then. Little is known of Mr. Bell's origins.

title: 100% Completion (RDR2)
text:
100% Completion is an accomplishment in Red Dead Redemption 2 that unlocks an achievement/trophy.
100% Completion is achieved when a set of designated tasks has been completed by the player in Story Mode. The following list provides the specific requirements for achieving 100% completion.
Tracking Progress
If at any point you want to check on your progress for this achievement, pause your game and go to Progress > Total Completion.
Missions And Events
Complete all 107 story missions required to finish the story.
Complete any 10 stranger mission strands.
Complete any 5 bounty hunter missions.
Complete 25 random encounters.
Survive a gang ambush.
Clear 6 gang hideouts.
Collectibles
Find any 1 Point of Interest.
Visit all 9 graves of your fallen companions. (Available only after story completion)
Collect 1 complete set of Cigarette Cards.
Complete "A Test of Faith".
Complete "A Fisher of Fish".
Complete "Duchesses and other Animals".
Complete "Geology for Beginners".
Complete "A Better World, A New Friend".
Complete a Treasure Hunt chain.
Find all 20 Dreamcatchers.
Compendium
Discover any 50 animal species.
Discover any 10 Equipment items.
Discover any 10 fish species.
Discover all 6 gangs.
Discover any 10 horse breeds.
Discover any 20 plant species.
Discover 48 weapons.
Player
Reach Level 10 Health, Stamina, and Dead Eye.
Achieve level 4 Bonding with your Horse.
Complete all 90 Challenges.
Miscellaneous
Investigate any 5 shacks.
Kill any 5 Legendary Animals.
Play each table game at least once.
Interact with 5 special characters.
Take a bath at least once. (Available in hotels)
Watch a show.
Watch a live show at the Theater.
Craft 1 recipe from six different category types.
Complete a Home Robbery, a Shop Robbery, a Coach Robbery and a Train Robbery.
Upon reaching 100% completion, the player will be taken to an exclusive short cutscene along with its associated unique journal entry.
Train Robberies do not necessarily require the player to rob passengers. Simply stealing a can of food at the back will count and is easier to do undetected, thus preventing law enforcement from getting involved.
The maximum level of Health, Stamina and Dead Eye a player can reach without completing the Challenges is 8. The extra two levels can only be obtained through the purchase of reinforced equipment from the trapper after completing certain Challenges.

title: A Battle of Blood
text:
A Battle of Blood is one of the newspaper articles in Red Dead Redemption 2.
VETERANS REMEMBER FORT BRENNAND.
It was a gorgeous fort by all accounts, sat in the Roanoke Ridge, southwest of Van Horn, predating the war that was to destroy it. A Union garrison was long stationed there, as it had been since the region was the frontier, watching over the usually calm and tranquil river passage nearby. However, one quiet night during the war, this calm was shattered and the fort would be no more. Confederate soldiers climbed nearby trees and fired down into the fortress. They then battered and broke through the north gate, outnumbering the forces stationed there. Events descended into a massacre, the details of which are still contested. A memorial is planned for the site.

title: A Better World, A New Friend
text:
A Better World, A New Friend is a Stranger mission featured in Red Dead Redemption 2.
The player finds posters across the map requesting perfect animal carcasses for use in a Wildlife Art Exhibition. The carcasses are to be sent to Ms. L. Hobbs from a Post Office.
Picking up the first poster will start the first hunting request from a total of 5. The first four are available from Chapter 2, the fifth list and the rest of the mission can only be completed in the Epilogue. These consist of:
Hunting request 1 (Valentine)
Perfect Squirrel Carcass
Perfect Rabbit Carcass

Perfect Rat Carcass
Perfect Woodpecker Carcass
Hunting request 3 (Rhodes)
Perfect Chipmunk Carcass
Perfect Oriole Carcass
Perfect Robin Carcass
Perfect Opossum Carcass
Hunting request 4 (Saint Denis)
Perfect Sparrow Carcass
Perfect Songbird Carcass
Perfect Toad Carcass

All carcasses of one request must be obtained and mailed together at the Post Office; mailing them one by one is not allowed. For this reason, it is recommended to hunt the animal that must be carried on the saddle last, after all other carcasses of the request have been acquired. Otherwise it may spoil if hunting remaining animals takes too long. Pronghorn Horn Trinket can prevent the spoiling of the carcass, but it's only available in the Epilogue, or if the player uses complicated tricks to get into New Austin earlier.
Part I
After completing all of the hunting requests, the player can visit L. Hobbs at the Taxidermist House. Here, she rewards John Marston with the Squirrel Statue.
Part II
Once the player has completed the epilogue, they should place the squirrel atop the fireplace at Beecher's Hope. The statue will disappear multiple times (after saving and loading for instance) and the player will have to find it and return it every time. The locations in which the statue can be located are as follows:

title: A Bitter Means To the Bitter End
text:
A Bitter Means To the Bitter End is a Moonshiner story mission, featured in Red Dead Online.
Mission Overview
In a bid to sabotage the Braithwaite's rival moonshine operation, Maggie asks you to taint their stills and sour their latest batch.
The protagonist goes to gather ingredients listed by Maggie for preparing a mixture. The player needs to collect Oleander Sage and Creeping Thyme at two areas, and also has to hunt down an animal at one place in order to get Animal Fat by skinning it. With the complete recipe, they can craft Maggie's mixture that in necessary to spoil the Braithwaite's moonshine.
After making the mixture, the player heads to Butcher Creek to ruin the vats. Quietly taking out the guards allows the stills to be soured using the substance. However, if the player gets noticed, the Braithwaites don't risk selling the moonshine, so the player can only destroy the stills, resulting in explosions. Upon souring or blowing up the moonshine, the player returns to their moonshine shack.
Deaths

title: A Bright Bouncing Boy
text:
A Bright Bouncing Boy is a Stranger mission featured in Red Dead Redemption 2. The quest becomes available during Chapter 4.
Professor Marko Dragic can be found sitting on a pond in Saint Denis having an outburst. After being introduced, he recruits the protagonist to help him with a new remote-controlled boat that he wishes to showcase for some investors. When the investors arrive, they ask that someone with no understanding operate Dragic's machine, and the protagonist decided to help.
Once the boat is in the water, the machine operates entirely on radio waves and electricity. The pond is full of mines that must be avoided and battleships that must be sunk. During the showcase, Dragic discusses just how remarkable his breakthroughs are. After the first wave is destroyed, Dragic sets in some sailboats that move around the pond and are easier to sink. After the demonstration, the spectators are impressed by the potential of Dragic's inventions, however, not impressed enough to support the professor. Dragic will fail to negotiate, then he will angrily destroy the control device by throwing it into the water.
A few days later, the protagonist can visit Dragic's workshop located in the northeastern corner of the map during the night time to continue the mission. The professor is worried that someone is coming to rob him and speaks to the protagonist through a microphone while in hiding. After seeing who it is, he tells the protagonist about the trouble he is having with his experiment. He has the protagonist take three metal rods outside and try to capture electricity from the thunderstorm outside.
Once all three rods are placed, Dragic pulls a lever but nothing happens. Frustrated, he tells the protagonist to climb to the top of a metal tower and flip a few switches to initiate the capture. After doing so, it turns out Dragic wishes to use the electricity to power his own robot. The experiment begins and the robot takes a few steps forward before collapsing. Regardless, Dragic is happy with the results.
A few days later, the protagonist can visit his workshop again to see his fate. Dragic can be found dead in a pool of blood inside his lab. If the player then goes to the other side of the map in The Grizzlies, they will find his robot sitting in the snow on top of a mountain ledge overlooking Colter, quietly mumbling "Papa" to itself over and over. The player can shoot the robot or leave it.
Deaths
Marko Dragic - Killed by his robot creation.
Dragic's robot (optional) - Can be "killed" by Arthur/John.
Part I
"Marko Dragic demonstrates his latest invention, a remotely controlled boat, to a crowd of potential investors and one buffoon in Saint Denis."
Once the player gains control of the remote-controlled boat, they must fire torpedoes at all battleships that are marked with large red circles on the minimap. It is recommended to destroy the mines as well if the player starts to drift closely. After the first wave of boats is destroyed, a wave of sailboats will spawn and move. There are four boats in each of the two rounds.
Part II
Once the player receives the rods conductors for the electricity, they must go outside and use the detector to narrow down the exact spot to place them. The darkness may make it difficult to locate the spot, though the player may take as long as they need to find it. Afterwards, the player must climb the large metal transmission tower and flip various switches; the player should ensure that all of them are all facing down to be properly configured. A fast way to achieve this is pulling the levers in this order: Middle, left, right.
Part III
The player can revisit Dragic's workshop and loot the area. They can find various notes showing the inventor's true intentions. Afterwards, if the player uses the Electric Lantern, it will direct them to a location in the northwest Grizzlies, in the mountains near Colter, to find the robot responsible for killing the inventor.
Electric Lantern
Inventor's Note
Inventor's Plan
While playing as either Arthur Morgan or John Marston during the second part of the mission, they will reveal they never went to school.
After completing Part I as Arthur, the player can meet Dragic as John in the Epilogue. If John does the second part of the stranger mission, he will explain to Dragic that his friend "helped him at the pond" years ago.
When placing the electric conductors, a pack of wolves can be seen in the distance and will be struck by lightning and killed. Curiously, the player can still skin them and their pelts will be in perfect condition in spite of the damage.
The remote control boat is a reference to the Teleautomaton, a remote-controlled submarine designed and built by Nikola Tesla in 1898.
Marko Dragic's robot appears to be a reference to the robot Elektro, the first robot in history, which was built in 1938 by Westinghouse Electric & Manufacturing Company, the company for which Tesla had served as an engineer.

qa_pairs.answer: Dragic wants to showcase his new remote-controlled boat to the investors.

qa_pairs.answer: After the investors leave, Dragic angrily destroys the control device by throwing it into the water.

title: A Cautionary Tale
text:
A Cautionary Tale is one of the newspaper articles in Red Dead Redemption 2.
RAILROAD PATH BRINGS DECLINE.
TUMBLEWEED RESIDENTS FRET AT FUTURE.
The once-bustling town of Tumbleweed in Gaptooth Ridge, New Austin, is growing quiet. The shops sit mostly empty. The blacksmith is idle. The population is dwindling as wagon after wagon of families leave. Since the railroad bypassed Tumbleweed in favor of Armadillo, trade and commerce has moved away.
The last holdouts fear that there exists not much future for their dear town of Tumbleweed and it will become another casualty of the technological advances that have blighted so much of our westward expansion, with controversial Sheriff Samuel Freeman presiding over a dusty, soon to be forgotten, relic in the desert.

title: A Day's Walk Poem
text:
A Day's Walk Poem is one of the letters in Red Dead Redemption 2.
It can be found in the Vetter's Echo cabin, just east of Pronghorn Ranch.
I wake on Owanjila's shore, and bathe.
And watch: the daylight kindles yellow fire
Above the dam, and soon ignites a swathe
Of eastern pines, until the lake's a pyre
Of blood red waters, yellow, gold, then blue
Once more. I pack my tent, and join the trail
Beside the river, heading north, the dew
Still wet upon the grass, the light still pale.
Here Canis latrans hunts Leporidae,
Crotalus atrox lurks in longer grass,
And once, I saw the distant amber eye
Of Ursus horribilis watch me pass.
And I among them, Homo sapiens:
Student not master; brother, not their lord.
Amid these fragrant pines, my blood transcends
Myself: an ancient kinship is restored.
Uphill the trees grow bare, seared long ago
By some forgotten fire. The trails turn north.
Soon I can see old Hagen capped with snow,
Across a tide of lupines rolling forth,
And there I leave the path, stretch out my hands,
And wade for home across the valley floor.
And yet, there's something missing from these lands.
Oh come, my Annabella - I implore!

title: A Fifth Person Slain
text:
A Fifth Person Slain is one of the newspaper artciles in Red Dead Redemption 2.
PATTERN IDENTIFIED.
MESSAGE SCRAWLED IN BLOOD.
WORRIES INTENSIFY OF PLAGUE.
SIMILAR TO DEATHS YEARS AGO.
Residents of Saint Denis are living in fear as the ritualistic deaths from years ago have returned. The pattern is the same. Teeth marks like those of a hyena or dog on the body are noticeable. There are messages scrawled next to the body in blood. Some had attributed the deaths to yellow fever, but others cite vampires as the cause. Saint Denis lawmen announced years ago they had caught the culprit and indeed did hang Bosco Lopez, who had spent many years living in Argentina before arriving in Saint Denis by frigate.
Now that the fifth victim has been found, lawmen are expressing caution, indicating that all residents should avoid traveling alone in the evening wherever possible, and keep all residences without locks barricaded overnight. Women are especially advised to show caution, as they are more often than not the victims of attacks.

title: A Fine Night For It
text:
A Fine Night For It is a Stranger mission featured in Red Dead Redemption 2. The quest becomes available during Chapter 2.
After encountering the Night Folk at least once, a stranger will appear on the road heading into Lagras during the night. A old man is sitting at a camp and tells the player about the Night Folk - a murderous group of killers who roam the Bayou. He tells the player that the Night Folk have overrun his house and asks the player to help him evict them. The player follows him to his house to help clear Night Folk off the property. During the walk, the stranger points to corpses, saying the Night Folk have made their mark here.
After reaching the house, the player will find five enemies and must fight them. After killing them, another group of four will spawn outside soon after and attempt to attack the cabin. After killing all enemies, the old man reclaims his house and gives a reward.
Availability: Complete one of the "Torch Procession", "Stalking Shadows", "Spooked Horse". or "Voice" chance encounters; mission available between 10pm and 5am only.
Walkthrough: After completing any of the chance encounters listed above, head to this stranger at night time - he has set up camp in the Bayou, just northwest of Lagras. Listen to his story and agree to help him. Follow him until you reach his property. A handful of Night Folk occupy the area: take the first one by surprise. then pick off the others as they sprint in your direction with instant headshots. After you enter the house, reinforcements arrive. Take cover behind the railing and dispatch them one by one. prioritizing those who wield machetes - these can potentially kill you with a single blow.
Deaths
Numerous members of the Night Folk - killed by Arthur/John and the Old Cajun.
Liberty Hat
The mission screen displays a different PED used for the Old Cajun than the one used in the final version of the game.
This mission is one of the two opportunities to grab the Liberty Hat, with the other being in the mission "An American Pastoral Scene". It is found on the head of a hogtied man next to the cabin near the end of the mission. Players should kill the Night Folk but refrain from entering the cabin to accept their reward, and instead check if the man wears the hat. If he doesn't, the player can reload the checkpoint.
After the wave of Night Folk, the player can free a hogtied man for a boost of honor if he is still alive at that point.

qa_pairs.answer: The old man tells the player about the Night Folk, a murderous group of killers who roam the Bayou.

qa_pairs.question: Where does the old man ask the player to go?
qa_pairs.answer: The old man asks the player to go to his house to help clear the Night Folk off the property.

qa_pairs.answer: After the player kills the initial enemies, reinforcements arrive and more Night Folk spawn outside to attack the cabin.

title: A Fine Night of Debauchery
text:
Javier: "And... how exactly are we getting out of here?"
Arthur: "I ain't too sure. This is what tends to happen when you leave Trelawny in charge of planning. All garnish, no meat."
―Javier and Arthur
A Fine Night of Debauchery is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
While at the Mayor's party, the Van der Linde gang learned of a poker tournament being held on the Grand Korrigan riverboat at the docks in Saint Denis. Leopold Strauss and Josiah Trelawny fix a game so Arthur Morgan can win big on the tables.
Arthur meets Trelawny in Saint Denis. Trelawny informs Arthur that in order to get on the riverboat, he'll need to smarten up. He takes Arthur to the tailor's the buy a new suit, then to the barber for a trim. Trelawny informs Arthur that their mark is Desmond Blythe and that Blythe keeps extra collateral in the safe in the Grand Korrigan. Afterwards, they ride to the riverboat in a carriage, and Trelawny informs Arthur of the plan, and tells him his cover is that he's an oil man. Trelawny also tells Arthur that the driver of the carriage and the dealer are now allies of his.
After arriving, Arthur leaves his weapons in the carriage, and walks to the boat along with Trelawny, Strauss, and Javier Escuella. Once on the boat, the four split up, while Arthur heads to the tables. He starts playing, with Strauss subtly conveying what he should do. With Strauss' help, Arthur quickly becomes the only player in the game besides Blythe, who causes the other players to go bust. Arthur beats Blythe in the next round, but Blythe challenges Arthur to a second game, putting his valuable Reutlinger Pocket Watch on the line. Arthur accepts, and quickly beats Blythe again. The pit boss congratulates Arthur on his victory and takes him upstairs to the vault, with Javier leading the way, disguised as a guard. Once the safe is open, Javier knocks out another guard, and holds the pit boss at gunpoint. Arthur disarms him, but while looting the safe, it is revealed that he has another gun.
Arthur quickly kills him and loots the safe, receiving a big take and Blythe's watch, and the duo move back to the bar, where Blythe is seen talking to Trelawny and accuses Arthur of cheating in the game. Suddenly, the guard whose clothes were taken by Javier appears and yells for the latter to be shot, causing a gunfight to erupt. After fighting their way to the deck, Arthur, Javier, Strauss, and Trelawny jump off the boat and swim to shore.
Upon reaching safety, the four share the take. After Strauss confirms that the stolen watch is valuable, Arthur takes it back, and the group split up.
Gold Medal Objectives
Win the game of Poker without Strauss’s help.
After your cover is blown, escape the boat in under 35 seconds.
Get 5 headshots.
Complete the mission without taking any health items.
Gold Medal Tips
For the first Gold Medal Objective, players must forfeit their first hand as it is always a losing hand. Go All-In on the second and third hands as the dealers rigged the game to favor you for the robbery, noting from Trelawny's hint earlier.
For the second Gold Medal Objective, kill every lawman with normal Dead Eye shots instead of tagging shots. This will save the player lots of time to escape and complete the time restraint requirement.
Mission Failure
The mission will fail if the player:
Assaults, kills or abandons Javier, Trelawny or Strauss;
Allows Javier, Trelawny or Strauss to be killed;
Loses the Poker game;
Alerts the law;
Destroys or disables George's carriage;
Jumps overboard;
Spooks the tailor;
Dies.
Deaths
Grand Korrigan guards - Killed by Arthur and Javier when escaping.
Grand Korrigan Pit Boss - Killed by Arthur.
Completing this mission unlocks the High Roller Double-Action Revolver.
The other three poker players who go bust in the first round are shown to be named Theodore Dixon, Perry Eastep, and Owen Gillies.
Looting the corpses of the killed guards after the shootout at the bar will reduce the player's honor.
Sometime after completing the mission, a random man in Saint Denis may notice that Arthur looks similar to who he saw on the boat. If so, he confronts Arthur about it, and Arthur can try to defuse the situation or antagonize the man. Regardless, he continues to believe that Arthur is responsible for the robbery, but leaves instead of notifying police.

text:
A Fisher of Fish is a Stranger mission in Red Dead Redemption 2. The quest becomes available after completion of the mission "A Fisher of Men".
Part I
Jeremy Gill, a self-proclaimed legendary fisherman, is found fishing off the dock. After he is approached, he asks if the player is interested in an autograph or photograph before leading them inside his cabin to show off his livelihood - selling stuffed fishes. He gives the player a map of all Legendary Fish sites in the world and says he'll pay a handsome price for any that are sent his way.

title: A Fisher of Men
text:
A Fisher of Men is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
Arthur does a favor for Abigail and takes Jack out on a fishing trip.
Arthur speaks to Abigail in camp, who asks him to do something fun with Jack, as he seems rather bored. Arthur is reluctant at first, but soon agrees. He heads over to Jack and greets him as he is playing in the grass. He invites Jack to come fishing with him. Jack seems interested, so Arthur mounts his horse and lifts Jack up so they can go. On the way, Jack asks Arthur if they are going back to the gang's previous campsite near Blackwater, as he left his Penny Dreadful storybook there. Arthur tells they can't go back, but promises to find Jack a new storybook.
Once at the river, the two start fishing, during which Jack decides to pick some flowers and make something. Once Arthur catches at least three fish, Jack shows him a necklace he made out of the flowers, but then two Pinkertons interrupt. They introduce themselves as Agents Milton and Ross. They explain that they were dispatched to find the gang after the robbery of one of Leviticus Cornwall's trains near Granite Pass, and that they want Dutch. Arthur tries to play innocent, but Milton says that he has already seen the "philosophy lesson" from Mac Callander, whom he had captured and tortured to death after the skirmish in Blackwater. Arthur is infuriated and exchanges hostile words with Milton before the two agents leave.
On the way back to camp, Jack asks why Arthur lied about Dutch and what the agents said about Mac. Arthur hopes that Mac is "fine where he is" and tells Jack to not worry about the "disagreeable men". After returning Jack to Abigail, Arthur heads over to Dutch to tell him about Milton and Ross and asks what they should do. Dutch believes that the Pinkertons want to scare them, and decides that they should all do nothing and just stay calm.
Dialogue
A Fisher of Men/dialogues
Gold Medal Objectives
After arriving at the river, catch a fish within 1 minute and 30 seconds.
Complete within 7 minutes and 20 seconds.
Gold Medal Tips
Due to the time limit requirement, it's recommended for the player to stop fishing and go to Jack once he sits down with the flower necklace.
Deaths
Mac Callander (off-screen) - Killed by Agent Milton and the Pinkertons after being captured during the Blackwater Massacre. Milton tells Arthur about this, describing his death as "slow, but merciful".
Mission Failure
The mission will fail if the player:
Alerts the law;
Fails to take Jack to the fishing area.
Video Walkthroughs
PS4 Version
PC Version
The name of the mission may be a reference to Matthew 4:19 and Mark 1:17, "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
When asked why Abigail chose Arthur in the opening cutscene, she can give two different lines, saying that Jack likes him or because he does what he says. This is seemingly random and not determined by the player's honor level.
Furthermore, if Arthur doesn't immediately go to Jack and hangs around Abigail, she will comment on Jack's needs for entertainment, as well as his location.
If the player rides slow enough, Arthur will point out the local wildlife.
If Arthur tramples an animal with his horse, Jack will comment on it.
The player cannot crash their horse into objects such as trees, nor fall/jump off cliffs in the typical fashion where Arthur falls off the horse, due to how Jack would also fall off: the player cannot injure nor see Jack injured during the mission. Attempting to go off a cliff while on horseback will immediately cause a "Failed" screen before the player becomes airborne, with the message "Jack was frightened".
If the player crosses the deeper part of the Dakota River with Jack on horseback, the mission will fail stating that the player's horse has died.
While fishing, Arthur may allude to his son, Isaac. He tells Jack while fishing that he taught another boy to fish a long time ago. When Jack asks if it was Lenny, Arthur says it wasn't, clarifying that it was long before he met Lenny and long before Jack's birth.
During the mission, Agent Milton curses Arthur for rejecting the offer to hand Dutch over, saying of the Van der Linde gang, "You people venerate savagery, and you will die... savagely... all of you!" Arthur later remembers the last part of Milton's quote during "A Fork in the Road" if his Honor is low.
At the end of the confrontation, as Milton and Ross return to their horses, the player can see that Arthur is about to draw his gun to shoot them, only avoiding so because of Jack's presence. This is considered a major "what if" moment, because if Arthur killed them during this mission, it would have altered the following events of Redemption 2 and Redemption, if not making the latter impossible.
This mission can be considered an echo to the ending of Redemption. During the fishing trip, Jack meets Agent Ross for the first time, next to a river. Years later, in revenge of his father's death, Jack kills Agent Ross when the latter is hunting ducks next to a river, thus concluding the storyline of Redemption. Ross even foreshadows his own death when he says, "Enjoy your fishing, kid... while you still can."
In this mission, Agent Milton also foreshadows his own death: when Arthur says, "Oh, we're all gonna die, Agent," he says in response, "Some of us sooner than others." In the final mission that the player plays as Arthur, Milton is killed by Abigail when he tries to kill Arthur, thus dying before him.
After returning to camp and informing Dutch of Agent Milton and Ross, Hosea will also approach Arthur asking about the Pinkertons.
If the mission is started at night, a slightly different cutscene will occur, where Arthur says he will take Jack fishing in the morning, before heading to bed. The mission continues as normal when he wakes up.
If Arthur had previously bought Jack new clothes, he will thank Arthur for the new pants while fishing.
While Jack and Arthur are fishing, Milton and Ross' horses are spawned in behind them but are invisible. Despite the player being unable to interact with them, it is still possible to search the saddlebags and get kicked down by an invisible horse.

title: A Fork in the Road
text:
A Fork in the Road is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Once Arthur arrives near the quest's area, in Saint Denis, he (will dismount if he's on a horse) starts coughing heavily until he passes out. He wakes up to find a stranger dragging and helping him to the local doctor's office, where he is greeted by a spooked receptionist, prompting her to call on doctor Joseph R. Barnes, who brings him into his surgery room. Before he starts examining him, he asks for a payment in order to help him, which Arthur quickly gives.
After an examination of his ear, breathing, and mouth, Arthur is then given the diagnosis of tuberculosis. Upon hearing the bad news, Arthur expresses disbelief. The doctor informs him that tuberculosis is a progressive disease, but stops himself before telling Arthur he will die. He gives Arthur advice to go somewhere warm and dry. Arthur responds with sarcasm and says it isn't possible, then begins to get up and leave.
Before leaving, Dr. Barnes injects a syringe with steroids into Arthur's arm, in order to give him "a little bit more energy" for the day. Arthur subsequently exits the surgery and falls into a trance, remembering various quotes from people that differ according to Honor level.
High Honor: The colour scheme of Arthur's trance is golden yellow, reflecting sunlight. The quotes Arthur recalls are positive, reassuring and reflective, with somber music. At the end, Arthur sees a buck in the distance that gazes at him before running away and disappearing.
Low Honor: The colour scheme of the trance is grey, reflecting fog. The quotes that Arthur recalls are negative, foreboding and defeatist, with ominous music. At the end, Arthur sees a coyote gazing at him in the distance before scarpering away and vanishing.
Gold Medal Objectives
Complete within 3 minutes and 5 seconds.
Gold Medal Tips
Due to the mission's Time Limit, after Arthur gets diagnosed and exits the doctor's office, players should take the road on the left and walk straight till they reach the crossroads and end the mission.
Video Walkthroughs
PS4 Version
PC Version
Background Music Played in the Mission
"Doctor's Opinion" - Played when Arthur is diagnosed with tuberculosis.
Once this mission is completed, Arthur will be sick with tuberculosis for the remainder of his playthrough, which will increase the core draining speed by 20%. He will also gain a limited amount of benefits from food and drinks, resulting in only coughing and a pop-up reminder of being sick if he has too much. The only way to fully refill any cores if fully empty while sick is to sleep. Additionally, Arthur will lose his stocky appearance and will look underweight, even at perfect weight, after this mission.
During this mission, when Arthur discovers that he has tuberculosis, Dr. Barnes comforts him with a line that Arthur will remember on his final ride in the "Red Dead Redemption" mission if his honor is high: "I'm really sorry for you, son, it's a hell of a thing."
One of the lines that Arthur remembers in this mission if his honor is high is "If we don't stop soon we'll all be dying", said by Hosea in "Outlaws from the West." However, Arthur wasn't present when Hosea said this, so he therefore wouldn't remember it.
If Arthur does not have any money on him, the Good Samaritan will give him ten dollars so that he can pay for the doctor visit. This also happens on mission replays.
This is one of the only missions that isn't marked on the map. It is triggered when visiting Saint Denis, typically as the player is attempting to meet Sadie Adler for the mission "Icarus and Friends.”
The name of the mission is a metaphor for a deciding moment in life or history, when a major choice of options is required.
If the player returns to the clinic after Arthur’s diagnosis, Dr. Barnes will regularly ask Arthur how he feels.

title: A Kind and Benevolent Despot
text:
A Kind and Benevolent Despot is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
With the help of a local, Gloria, Dutch and Arthur infiltrate Fussar's compound to rescue Javier.
Arthur meets Dutch at a narrow ledge in a cliff. Dutch hands Arthur a flaming torch and they slowly make their way across the cliff. Arthur asks where they are going to go after leaving Guarma and Dutch says that they will head back to Saint Denis in the US, as that is the least place anyone will expect them to go. Arthur is baffled and skeptical at this idea despite Dutch's reassurances. The duo arrive at the entrance to a cave, where they are greeted by an old woman named Gloria, who Dutch pays in gold to guide them through the cave.
As they head through the cave, Arthur asks what else happened during the bank robbery that he never saw, and Dutch wonders with suspicion why Hosea and Lenny were both killed but John was spared and imprisoned and how Abigail managed to escape. Upon reaching a ladder, Gloria demands more money, but Dutch had already paid her with the last gold bar he had. She pulls a knife on him, but she is uncharacteristically choked to death by Dutch, much to Arthur's shock and dismay.
As they climb up the ladder, Arthur questions Dutch's murderous actions and Dutch replies that he will do whatever it takes to ensure that the gang survive. Outside Aguasdulces, they see Javier being dragged by a donkey and mocked by Colonel Fussar and his soldiers. After killing two guards, the pair sneak into the refinery and sabotage the compound sugar production, ripping open bags of sugar and setting the place on fire with the furnace to create a distraction. After the building explodes, they free Javier and fight their way out of the compound. With Dutch carrying an unconscious Javier, they run through the sugar fields while Arthur holds off the men chasing them.
They cross a small stream, and Dutch tells Arthur to hold off the men, then meet him at the fortress in Cinco Torres. Arthur kills the last of the men and departs.
Gold Medal Objectives
Get Javier to safety in under 2 minutes.
Get 10 headshots.
Gold Medal Tips
For the first Gold Medal objective, rush ahead of Dutch when he goes to grab Javier to initiate the escape and clear out any soldiers spawning in. Stay close to Dutch, or else he will stop and waste valuable time.
When players reach the sugar fields, it's recommended for them to strictly stay behind Dutch and only take down soldiers who start to show up behind Arthur (the minimap will show red dot icons).
Players should limit their Dead Eye usage, as entering Dead Eye for too long will cause time loss. It's recommended to tag some soldiers and then fire immediately instead of trying to tag every soldier.
Deaths
Gloria - Strangled to death by Dutch van der Linde for demanding more money and brandishing a knife at him.
Numerous Guarma guards - Killed by Arthur Morgan and Dutch van der Linde.
Sun Hat
Depending on Arthur's honor, there will be slightly different dialogue between him and Dutch after Gloria is killed:
If Arthur's honor is high, he will remind Dutch that he keeps killing people and asks if he will strangle him next after they climb outside.
If Arthur's honor is low, he will simply ask if Dutch is alright and that the gang have probably all gone rotten.
Oddly, neither Dutch nor Arthur stop to retrieve the gold bar stolen from the Saint Denis bank following Gloria's death.
If the player returns to Gloria, they will find that she cannot be looted despite the minimap showing her dead.
If the player vaults the wall they face upon exiting the refinery, they can freely explore the entire Guarma area without failing the mission as long they don't produce any noise through firepower.
If the player tries to shoot at Fussar or any of his soldiers after the cutscene plays, the mission will fail and there will be another cutscene where Javier gets killed by the guards. Even if the player manages to kill all the guards using trainers or external scripts, two guards will spawn to shoot Javier, leading to a failure.
If "Savagery Unleashed" is done before this mission, Arthur will tell Dutch that the situation with the workers is done with. If done before "Savagery Unleashed", Dutch will ask Arthur if he saved the workers in which Arthur will say he will afterwards.
If the player tries to return to the entrance of the cave system that Arthur and Dutch use at the beginning of the mission after the mission's completion, they will be shot by an invisible sniper while they try to make their way across the extended narrow ledge that leads to the cave entrance.
After completing the mission, if the player returns to Aguasdulces and climbs back down the ladder at the end point of the tunnel system, Gloria's body will have vanished, while the metal gate that Dutch and Arthur open during the mission will once again be firmly locked.
If "Savagery Unleashed" is completed before this mission, the mission "Hell Hath No Fury" will start automatically.

title: A New Future Imagined
text:
A New Future Imagined is the penultimate mission of the epilogue and overall storyline in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
John and Abigail go in to Blackwater to spend some quality time together. John has a question to ask her.
The mission starts with Abigail bickering with Uncle about his lousy work ethic. Abigail and John then decide they need to take a break from the farm and go out with each other for some alone time with each other. Before they can leave the ranch, Duncan and Angus Geddes arrive, delivering old furniture to the Marstons' ranch in Beecher's Hope in gratitude for John saving Pronghorn Ranch from the Laramie Gang, much to John's and Abigail's appreciation. They go to Benjamin P. Lockhart's Photo Studio in Blackwater to take a photo, before entering the Imperial Theatre to view a "moving picture". Finally, John and Abigail borrow a canoe and row to the middle of the Blackwater lake, where John finally proposes to Abigail. Surprised, Abigail agrees to marry him and the two kiss.
The next morning, John leaves Abigail's bedside while she's asleep and then walks outside toward the fence to watch the sunrise.
Gold Medal Objectives
Complete within 7 minutes and 30 seconds.
Mission Failure
The mission will fail if the player:
Assaults, kills, or abandons Abigail;
Spooks Abigail;
Alerts the law;
Attacks or kills their horse;
Dies.
Gallery
John and Abigail riding to Blackwater.
Video Walkthroughs
PS4 Version
PC Version
Abigail says she has never seen a film, and John reacts with incredulity. This is strange as cinema would have been unheard of in the West prior to their meeting in 1894, and since leaving the gang in 1899 they have spent almost every waking moment together, meaning that John would be well aware of this.
At the start of the mission, if John does not interfere in Uncle and Abigail's conversation, the game will make the player walk to them by itself.
Several aspects of this mission have similarities with Arthur Morgan's experiences:
John and Abigail going to the theater mirrors what Arthur and Mary Linton decide to do while they are together in Saint Denis. Also, when John gets the ring at the start, he is also holding a picture of young Arthur and Mary.
John saying "It would make me very happy" is very similar to Arthur's high-Honor line "It would mean a lot to me" when urging Marston to run and find his family during the mission "Red Dead Redemption" (if the player went with John). Incidentally, this mission is also based around John being with his family.
This mission ends with John on the ranch watching the sunrise, which is the final thing Arthur sees if he died with high Honor.
There is an unused cutscene for this mission where John and Abigail can be seen arriving at Beecher's Hope.
The mission icon features John with his NPC hair, which is impossible to use in-game.

title: A New Jerusalem
text:
A New Jerusalem is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
John puts together his pre-cut ranch house with the help of Charles and the encouragement of Uncle.
John, Charles and Uncle decide to work together to assemble the house. Uncle uses his 'terminal lumbago' as an excuse to get out of doing the actual work and instead contents himself with giving the orders.
John and Charles assemble the house over the course of several weeks - first placing the joists to build the foundation, then hammering in the joists, raising the house frame and finally placing the tiles for the rooftop. Once the house is finished, the trio raise a toast to John's new home.
Later, John writes a letter to Abigail informing her of his reunion with Charles and Uncle, their help in the acquisition and construction of his newly-purchased land and house, and tries to convince her that he has changed his former ways, and misses her and Jack dearly.

title: A Quick Favor for an Old Friend
text:
John Marston: "A barn will take three of us six months to build!"
Uncle: "Oh, you don't build a barn, dumbass. What do you think this is, 1785? You buy one pre-cut, just like the house."
―Uncle and John talking about building a barn for the ranch.
A Quick Favor for an Old Friend is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
With his debts mounting and a barn to buy, John accompanies Sadie to hunt down the wanted criminal, Ramón Cortez, and bring him to justice.
John finds Uncle resting under a tree. John yells at Uncle for being lazy and Uncle asks John if he believes in reincarnation and John states that he does not believe in that. Uncle complains about his condition, but John tells him to help out with farming. Uncle tells John that the land is good for grazing and suggests that John will need to get a barn if he wants to buy livestock. John believes that building a barn will take at least six months, so Uncle suggests that he could buy a pre-cut barn and they head over to the lumber yard. John greets Albert Cakes and tells him that he needs a barn, so Albert opens a catalogue of pre-cut buildings and John picks out one. John and Uncle thank Cakes for the help.
John and Uncle head to the bank, where Ansel Atherton tells John that he wants to help him but can not help give him another loan and gets annoyed by Uncle's behavior. The pair leave and John yells at Uncle for being annoying to Atherton. Sadie appears and greets them. John asks Sadie if she has any work as he needs money to pay off his loan to the bank. Sadie states that she has a job and it's dangerous. Sadie lets John join her. Sadie states she received a bounty she is after is located at Painted Sky. She states that she received a tip from an encyclopedia salesman, who went to the property to look for the rancher to sell an encyclopedia, but saw a Mexican man on the property. Sadie tells John that the bounty she is going after is Ramón Cortez, a wanted Del Lobo gang member. Sadie and John talk during the travel, discussing the Skinner Brothers and John's new house. Once they arrive at Painted Sky, Sadie suggests to John to split up. Sadie heads to the house while John heads to the barn.
Sadie finds Wróbel tied to a chair and she unties him. Wróbel states that Cortez is hiding in the barn. When John enters the barn, Cortez ambushes him and the two men fight. John defeats him and Cortez surrenders. Sadie rushes over to John and hits Cortez with her shotgun. John carries the unconscious Cortez and places him on Sadie's horse. Sadie tells John that they are going to Scarlett Meadows Sheriff's Office in Rhodes. John is surprised by this and Sadie states that the environment there has changed. Cortez wakes up and attempts to bribe them to let him go and Sadie tells him to shut up.
They eventually arrive, Sadie heads to the sheriff office and tells John to bring Cortez. Cortez attempts to bribe John to kill Sadie, but John tells him to shut up. Sadie greets Sheriff Thomas and tells him that they have Cortez. Sheriff Thomas is pleased that they were able to capture Cortez. John places him into the cell and Cortez attempts to bribe all of them to let him go, but Sheriff Thomas tells Cortez that he and his deputies are taking him to Saint Denis to be hanged for his crimes. Sheriff Thomas tells Sadie and John to help him guard Cortez until his deputies arrive. Sheriff Thomas offers the two drinks and Cortez is seen laughing inside his cell. As they wait for the deputies, it becomes nighttime and Sadie and John rest.
The next day, John and Sadie wake up. The Del Lobo Gang arrive in Rhodes and demand Sheriff Thomas to release Cortez or they will kill them. John, Sadie and Sheriff Thomas fight the gang members in the town and defeat them. Sadie and John hear an explosion and rush over. Sheriff Thomas tells them that a Del Lobo blew a hole in the cell and Cortez escaped. Sadie tells Sheriff Thomas to give them the bounty money, even though Cortez escaped. Sheriff Thomas states that he does not have the money and will not get the money if he does not bring Cortez to Saint Denis. Sheriff Thomas tells them to get Cortez back and that he will add an extra $50 to Cortez's bounty, though he and Sadie haggle to $75 extra. Sadie and John search the area and Sadie spots a campsite and notices the gang members. Sadie tells John to come with her to the old water mill to get a vantage view.
Sadie notices that they are waiting for a boat. Sadie tells John she is going down to the campsite and that she will take care of the gang members. John provides sniper support from the mill and Sadie then calls to John to come down to help her. Sadie and John fight the gang members and they notice that Cortez is escaping in a row boat. John shoots at the boat, which forces Cortez to row the boat back to land. John ties Cortez up and John notices more gang members. Cortez sees them and calls out to them in Spanish. They defeat the remaining gang members and take Cortez back to Rhodes. Sadie calls out to the sheriff that they got him and John hands over Cortez to the deputies. Cortez is placed in a jail wagon. Sheriff Thomas tells them that they will get their money once he and his deputies arrive in Saint Denis. The sheriff and deputies leave with Cortez. Sadie thanks John and John asks her to send his money to the bank.
Gold Medal Objectives
Force Cortez's men to flee from Rhodes within 30 seconds.
Get 5 headshots while covering Sadie with a long scoped rifle.
Get 4 hip fire kills.
Complete the mission without taking any health items.
Gold Medal Tips
The hardest challenge for this mission is the "hip fire kills" requirement. Hence, it's recommended for players to equip with shotguns to perform a hip fire right at the start of the ambush.
On Replays, it's recommended to perform a few hip fires with the strongest pistol when there're two or three of Cortez's men near John during the ambush, then do the hip-fire during the attack on Cortez's gang to capture him.
Use any high damage weapon to kill Cortez's men as fast as possible.
Mission Failure
The mission will fail if the player:
Assaults, kills, or abandons Sadie, Uncle or Sheriff Thomas;
Allows Sadie or Sheriff Thomas to be killed;
Kills or abandons Cortez;
Allows Cortez to escape;
Alerts the law;
Kills or abandons their horse;
Dies.
Deaths
Various Del Lobo gang members - Killed by John Marston and Sadie Adler.
Before the mission starts, John can awake Uncle by firing a bullet next to him. This will cause him to awake and lock the mission for a short while.
Even if John already caught all the free roam bounties who are to be delivered at the Rhodes jail (Mark Johnson, etc.), his lines of dialogue will still read as if he had never been back to Rhodes since the epilogue started. He will also repeat the same lines of dialogue of the previous mission regarding him "doing some bounty hunting of his own" to Sadie, as if it were the first time she was told that.
Also, any bounty targets previously apprehended who may be awaiting the gallows in the Rhodes jail will disappear after this mission and their execution will never be played.
If John or Arthur has killed Flaco Hernández before this mission, John will reply to Sadie suggesting he has met Sheriff Freeman of Tumbleweed, even if the player has never ventured into New Austin or Tumbleweed.
This is likely an oversight tied to events when the player first meets the Del Lobo Gang as a part of "The Noblest of Men, and a Woman" Stranger Mission.
John can put Ramón Cortez on either Sadie's horse or his own, since the mission objective never specifies which horse to place him on.
If John ignores Sadie's instruction to check the barn at first, he can follow Sadie to find Wróbel tied to a chair, saying that Cortez is in the barn. Sadie will also comment on this.
After Cortez's escape from the jail, if incendiary buckshot is used on the Del Lobo gang members, John will become wanted by the law and the mission will automatically fail.
If Esteban Cortez is captured before completing this mission, and during the ride to Painted Sky, John will mention to Sadie that he met Sheriff Freeman and postulates that Esteban and Ramón are related, which Sadie confirms saying that they are brothers.
This mission is similar to the Red Dead Redemption mission Spare the Rod, Spoil the Bandit as in both missions, John checks a barn and a hostage(s) is saved from the main house.
If the player kills Ramón Cortez when he is rowing his boat to flee, Sadie will react and get mad at the player.
If the player takes a hat off one of the Del Lobos after the shootout at Rhodes, Sadie will comment that John has fallen on hard times that he needs to steal hats.
For this mission only, one of the graves at Rhodes Church has a hole that drops into the void below the map.
When John returns home to see the newly-built barn, a version of 'Dies Irae' plays. 'Dies Irae' is a musical representation of death, which alludes to John's death in The Last Enemy That Shall Be Destroyed.
During the mission, John says he thinks Mexico is a tough place. Sadie retorts that it's a very tough place for him. This is ironic because four years later, John will be a major factor in ending the civil war in Mexico.

title: A Quiet Time
text:
A Quiet Time is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
Arthur takes Lenny for a quiet drink in Valentine to help calm him down after learning of Micah's arrest in Strawberry.
Lenny arrives back at camp with the news that Micah was arrested in Strawberry for murder and that Sheriff Hanley is going to hang him. Dutch instructs Arthur to rescue Micah later and take Lenny into Valentine to calm him down. After arriving, the duo start drinking, until a patron named Jeb annoys the pair, and Arthur can either charm, intimidate, or assault him into leaving them alone. If the player does nothing, the charm button will automatically fill slowly until full.
After drinking some more, Arthur loses Lenny and begins looking for him, drunkenly stumbling around the saloon, and finds him upstairs, trying to balance a shot glass on his forehead (before dropping it over the railing, smashing it on the floor below). Reunited, the two start drinking again, but Arthur soon loses him again and after searching the bar a second time finds Lenny downstairs trying to fight off two men from atop the bar counter. Arthur confronts the men, but ends up drunkenly line dancing with the patrons of the bar. After relieving himself outside, Arthur returns to the bar to find Lenny for the third time, but he is so drunk and inebriated by this point that he sees every patron as Lenny (with jumbled-up button prompts and misspelled text to boot). After stumbling around, drunkenly yelling after Lenny and talking to three or more patrons, Lenny finds Arthur, and the pair engage in a slap fight before they return to drinking again. Jeb then re-enters the bar, and steals Arthur's drink out of his hand. This prompts Arthur to grab Jeb by the collar.
The game then cuts to Arthur and Lenny outside, holding Jeb over a water trough. At this point the player can do one of three things before a group of lawmen confront them to arrest the duo for their drunken shenanigans, leading to Lenny's arrest and Arthur fleeing, either escaping and fleeing the town or colliding with a barrel or tripping over a fence, falling over and being arrested as well. The option chosen will affect how the mission ends, with six different endings depending on what happens during these two moments.
Do nothing: if the player does not follow the button prompts to begin trying to drown Jeb in the water trough, he will break free and run away to retrieve the law.
Attempt to drown Jeb: if the player begins the button prompts to drown the patron, but doesn't complete it in time, Jeb breaks free and runs away, retrieving the law.
Drown Jeb: if the player completes the button prompt to drown Jeb, Arthur will drown Jeb until he is unconscious and then dump him onto the ground next to the trough, the law will then find Jeb there and begin searching for the pair.
Arthur escaped from the law, didn't force Jeb into the water trough: Arthur wakes up just south of the camp but is very hung over, gagging and vomiting onto the grass. He then returns to camp to find Lenny, who states he doesn't know what happened during their escape.
Arthur was arrested with Lenny, didn't force Jeb into water trough: Arthur and Lenny wake up in Valentine jail, charged with assault. After the pair post bail, they will pause outside the office, as Lenny vomits into the street, then go their separate ways back to camp.
Arthur escapes, attempted to drown Jeb: Arthur meets with Lenny back at camp, who was arrested and had to post bail for assault. Lenny then laments last night's events with Arthur, comparing it to Micah's actions in Strawberry.
Arthur was arrested with Lenny, attempted to drown Jeb: Arthur and Lenny wake up in Valentine jail, where they have been charged with assault. After the pair post bail, they will pause outside the office, as Lenny vomits into the street, then go their separate ways back to camp.
Arthur escapes, drowned Jeb: Arthur meets with Lenny back in camp, who was arrested for attempted murder and had to post bail. Lenny then laments last night's events with Arthur, comparing it to Micah's actions in Strawberry.
Arthur was arrested with Lenny, drowned Jeb: Arthur and Lenny wake up in Valentine jail, where they have been charged with attempted murder. After the pair post bail, they will pause outside the office, as Lenny vomits into the street, then go their separate ways back to camp.
Mission Failure
The mission will result in an automatic failure if the player does any of the following:
Assaults, kills, or abandons Lenny;
Allows Lenny to be killed;
Gets knocked out by Lenny;
Leaves Valentine;
Leaves the saloon area;
Alerts the law;
Kills or abandons their horse;
Dies.
Gold Medal Objectives
Try to make amends with an old rival
Catch Lenny in the act
Don't get arrested
Gold Medal Tips
After losing Lenny for the first time, Tommy can be seen sitting at a table eating by himself, near the pillar with the cattle skull. Talk to him four times to complete the first Gold Medal objective. He will not be present afterwards.
While searching for Lenny the third time and Arthur is hallucinating that all patrons are Lenny, go onto the second floor and walk into the far room on the left of the stair. A cutscene of Arthur walking in on a prostitute with a client (hallucinating that they are both Lenny), where they all scream at each other in horror before Arthur slams the door, will play. After the cutscene ends, the objective is complete. The objective cannot be triggered by attempting to enter the room earlier in the mission.
Keep running straight, then go right as soon as you get past the alleyway and climb when you reach the fence. Make sure not to collide with any of the pillars or anything else in the alleyway. (Warning: The button prompt to climb will be blurred out and will not become visible until the very last second). You will know you have succeeded when Arthur wakes up out in the wilderness and not in jail.

title: A Rage Unleashed
text:
Charles: "You know I told your father I will not fight over some horses."
Dutch: "But I made no such promise."
―Charles Smith and Dutch van der Linde to Eagle Flies
A Rage Unleashed is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
Eagle Flies and the gang launch a raid on an army boat, to reclaim horses stolen from the Wapiti Reservation.
In camp, Arthur approaches Reverend Swanson, and the two have a brief conversation. They are quickly interrupted by Dutch, who calls Arthur over to him. Dutch tells him that the gang will go north to New York before heading to the tropics. He explains his ideas regarding "smoke and commotion" and making the gang money, while Arthur instead says that the gang are "not so good at doing scores anymore" and is doubtful of Dutch's plans.
Suddenly, they are interrupted with the arrival of Eagle Flies, who is escorted into camp by Karen and Javier. Eagle Flies explains that the US Army have confiscated his tribe's horses, and that his people will "starve" if he doesn’t retrieve them, before going on to denounce the abduction of said horses as an "act of war". Charles tells him that, as he promised Rains Fall, he will not get involved in this conflict. Meanwhile, Dutch spontaneously decides to help him, and tells Eagle Flies to put his money away. Suspicious of Dutch's motives, Charles and Arthur decide to accompany the pair.
The group ride southeast, near to Copperhead Landing. On the way, Arthur questions Dutch on why he is helping Eagle Flies with this, despite seemingly having nothing to gain from it. Dutch, however, brushes this off and reminds him of the gang's motto, before later telling him that interfering in the Native Americans' conflict with the Army may divert attention away from the gang. The group arrive at their destination, and meet up with a few other Wapiti men, including Paytah. Before starting their mission, the group decide to wait until nighttime in order for them to sneak aboard the boat more easily thanks to the darkness.
With the arrival of night, the group silently row towards the ship, which is carrying the horses, and quietly board it. Once on it, they stealthily neutralize the soldiers on-board, including a group playing poker. Once this is done, Dutch begins to drive the ship towards the land. Unfortunately, though, he loses control and accelerates rapidly, before crashing. As a result, the ship begins to take on a large amount of water, and the gang are forced to free the horses and swim with them back to land. After leading most of them back to the riverbank, Eagle Flies asks Arthur to round up the remaining few. Arthur mounts one of these horses and, while leading two others, gets back to land by riding the swimming horse.
Upon arriving at the shore, Dutch offers to ride with Eagle Flies to take the horses back to the reservation while promising him that they will defeat the Army and save the Indians, leaving Arthur more worried than ever. After the two ride away, Charles asks Arthur to go and visit Rains Fall, which the player can either accept or decline.
Gold Medal Objectives
Knock out 2 soldiers on the boat.

Gold Medal Tips
Do not take out any weapons when ambushing the soldiers, or else Arthur will kill them instead of knocking them out.
Swim and jump on the closest horse, then sprint all the way to catch up with the time limit.

title: A Really Big Bastard
text:
A Really Big Bastard is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
Sadie visits John at Beecher's Hope. They leave to hunt down a bounty, Marshall Thurwell, in Tall Trees and discuss other men who have evaded their capture.
With his family now reunited at Beecher's Hope, John enters the living room to find Abigail knitting, one morning. He asks if she's pleased with his efforts, to which she responds that she's pleased, but doesn't forgive his past behavior in jest. Jack then calls his parents out to the front porch, to find that Sadie Adler has arrived to see them. Abigail, though confused as to how John knew Sadie had come, invites her in for lunch, overjoyed to see her again after 8 years.
Later, the group talk and eat together on the front porch. Abigail asks about Sadie's current job, learning that she works as a bounty hunter and gun-for-hire. Sadie attempts to offer a job to John to pay off his bank loans, assuring them that the work is safe, legal and well-paying. Initially, Abigail declines on John's behalf, but soon learns that John was doing exactly this, in his family's absence. John asserts that he desperately needed money and that bounty hunting was the only work he was capable of doing with his skills, but Abigail disapproves because of the danger it could bring to himself and the family, as well as the bad influence it could pose to Jack.
Sadie also reveals she's been tracking Micah down ever since his return to West Elizabeth. Abigail objects even more strongly to the prospect of hunting Micah, given how dangerous he is, his actions within the gang, and the gravity of the repercussions from confronting him. Sadie apologizes for mentioning Micah and backtracks to her original offer.
Abigail asks Sadie about the bounty: Marshall Thurwell, an accountant who robbed his employer in Rhodes and later fled to West Elizabeth. Sadie, once more, reassures Abigail that the job is low risk-high reward. Abigail relents and permits John to accompany Sadie on her bounty hunts, so long as he returns home safely, but maintains her stance on Micah. With Abigail's permission, John and Sadie head for Tall Trees. On the way there, Sadie praises John's efforts in building his ranch and reunion with his family. John also reveals that he intends to propose to and officially marry Abigail, with the engagement ring that Arthur had once proposed to Mary Linton with, long ago. Sadie expresses joy for John, noting how happy her own marriage made her.
Once at Tall Trees, they make their way to Thurwell's camp to search for any clues to his whereabouts, hoping that he hasn't been killed by the Skinner Brothers or the local wildlife. There, they find a set of tracks leading to a dilapidated cabin and find a man's mangled corpse, just outside. John and Sadie look upon the corpse, disturbed, wondering if he was their bounty or not. A voice calls out from the cabin, asking if "it" is gone. The pair aim their guns at the cabin, and ask if the man is Marshall Thurwell, which he confirms he is. Sadie states her intentions, who Thurwell is wanted by and why.
The pair order Thurwell to leave the cabin, to which he complies while asking if "the monster" is gone. Just as he exits, though, the aforementioned monster - revealed to be a giant, heavily scarred grizzly bear - comes out and charges at the pair, knocking them to the ground and frightening them. The bear then runs around and charges back at John, who tries to fire off as many rounds as he can from his gun, but is knocked to the ground, forced to fight for his life as the bear rips and tears at him. As soon as John manages to get the bear off of him, Sadie fires off a final warning shot, finally prompting the bear to clear off.
After the attack, Sadie helps John back on his feet, and go to deal with Thurwell once more. Both furious at what just transpired, and Thurwell's cowardice, Sadie knocks him out, and John ties him up. As the two head for Blackwater, they discuss the danger their work puts them in, with Sadie wondering if she should've brought John along, considering the consequences of any harm befalling him on his family. John reassures her that he took the job knowing the risks and needed the work. They also dispose of two bounty hunters who attempt to steal Thurwell from them, and discuss Micah. Sadie says that she should just take of him alone and that John should just be with his family and his new life, but John is determined to deal with Micah personally. Sadie tells him that rumor has it that Micah is not far away and promises to let John know where he is as soon as she hears something.
They arrive at the police station in Blackwater and drop off Thurwell. Sadie promises to send John's payment to the bank herself and John leaves.

title: A Short Walk in a Pretty Town
text:
A Short Walk in a Pretty Town is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2.
Mission Overview
Arthur, Micah, Bill and Sean go to meet some of the Gray boys in Rhodes to discuss a security job.
Arthur meets the other three gang members in Rhodes for the “job”, although both he and Sean are deeply suspicious. Before they can voice any more concerns, they are suddenly ambushed by the Grays. Sean is instantly killed by a shot to the head, and Bill is shot in the shoulder. A massive shootout erupts between the remaining three outlaws and the Gray gunmen.
During the gunfight, Bill is captured by Sheriff Leigh Gray, leaving only Arthur and Micah to fight off the Grays. Both of them break into the Gunsmith's and use it as cover. After the two come out victorious, they approach the Sheriff's office and demand the release of Bill. Along with Archibald MacGregor and two other lawmen, the Sheriff comes out with a gun to Bill's head but is promptly shot in the head and killed by Arthur. In the next few seconds, Archibald and his two allies are subsequently gunned down by Arthur, or by Micah if the player is not quick enough.
With the gunfight over, Arthur reprimands Bill and Micah for their carelessness and expresses his affection for Sean, before asking Bill to give Sean a proper burial.
Aftermath
Following this mission, Rhodes will be temporarily put on lockdown and the player will be unable to enter Caliga Hall without ensuring a shootout if spotted by the guards.
Gold Medal Objectives
Kill 3 lawmen in Dead Eye while saving Bill.
Complete using only sidearms.
Complete within 4 minutes 30 seconds.
Get 20 headshots.
Complete the mission without taking any health items.
Gold Medal Tips
It is advised you try to get to the side door of the Gunsmith as early as you can (alongside reaching your headshot requirements), in order to beat the strict time limit requirement for Gold, as this will trigger Micah to enter the store and speed up the next phase of the mission.
However, you can ignore Micah's request and rush through the front door. This will delay the second phase, but allow Arthur to kill the previous phase lawmen, ensuring 20 Headshots completion.
For the first Gold Medal objective, Dead Eye-tag the 3rd lawmen on the right first, then tag the 4th on the right and then the rest of the lawmen before firing. Arthur will most likely kill all of the lawmen or perfectly execute 3 of them.
Deaths
Sean MacGuire - Killed by a gunshot to the head from a Gray hired gun sniper.
Leigh Gray - Killed by Arthur Morgan while holding Bill hostage.
Archibald MacGregor - Killed by either Arthur or Micah after exiting the Sheriff’s Office.
Jock Gray - Killed by either Arthur or Micah after exiting the Sheriff's Office.
Rhodes Lawmen and Gray hired guns - Killed by Arthur, Micah and Bill during the shootout.
Mission Failure
The mission will fail if the player:
Kills Sean before his scripted death;
Assault, kills, or abandons Micah or Bill;
Allows Micah or Bill to be killed;
Dies.
When the mission becomes available, all shops in Rhodes will be closed temporarily. Players will be able to visit them again after completing the mission "The Battle of Shady Belle".
The Rhodes train station is also devoid of people. This serves as a sign of the incoming ambush by the Grays.
Blackjack can still be played in the saloon despite being mostly empty.
Sean's horse, Ennis, is not seen at the start of the mission, while Bill's and Micah's horses are present, serving as an implication that he will not make it out of the mission.
Shortly before the mission becomes available the player can observe Sean and Jack Marston in a random camp event in the Clemens Point camp that foreshadows that something bad is about to happen to Sean: Sean and Jack find a dead white rabbit to which Sean tells him that the rabbit is a sign, though he does not know of what. A white rabbit is generally considered to be a symbol of good luck, while encountering a dead white rabbit portends that someone's luck has run out.
During the final standoff, Arthur only needs to shoot Sheriff Gray; the three deputies would be shot by Micah before they can shoot him, Arthur or Bill.
It is also impossible to disarm Sheriff Gray or any of the deputies during the standoff, since any accurate shot will kill them instantly.
Depending on Arthur's honor, he will say something different at the end of the mission.
If Arthur's honor is high, he will say that he misses Sean and that he was like an annoying little brother to him and that they had great fun riding together.
If Arthur's honor is low, he will say that Sean has been killed in an ambush and that there is still no sign of the confederate gold.
Two Double-Barreled Shotguns can be found in this mission: the one from Sean's corpse, and another near the back door to the Gunsmith's.
When entering the Gunsmith's, the player is free to use the front entrance instead of the back without failing the mission, though Micah will be annoyed that his instructions were ignored.
The dynamite barrel outside the Gunsmith's cannot be destroyed during this mission.
Before this mission is unlocked, Arthur can be informed by either Dutch (if all the other missions are completed) or by Josiah (after the mission "Friends in Very Low Places") to meet Bill and the others in Rhodes.

title: A Strange Kindness
text:
Arthur: "Looks like I've turned into the goddamn errand boy."
Dutch: "You have turned into my son... you worry because I worry. We are just the same."
―Arthur Morgan and Dutch van der Linde
A Strange Kindness is a mission in Red Dead Redemption 2. It is the final mission of Chapter 2.
Mission Overview
Wanting the gang to lie low after the trouble in Valentine, Dutch asks Arthur and Charles to scout out a new camp location at Dewberry Creek.
After getting involved in a shootout in Valentine, Arthur rides back to camp to find the gang packing up. Dutch says that Micah told him of a good hideout spot at Dewberry Creek, and sends Arthur and Charles to check it out.
Upon reaching the dried-up creek, the pair notes it's a poor spot and they find a dead body in the riverbed. They soon find a small camp nearby and a German family hiding under a wagon. The family could hardly speak English. However, the daughter managed to communicate that the father had been kidnapped. Arthur doesn't want to look for him, but Charles convinces him, and the two ride off to search for the man.
They follow a horse trail and reach a clearing by Flat Iron Lake. They find the father tied up, but are attacked by bandits. Once the assault has been put down, Arthur unties the man and takes him back to his family. While riding back, he tells Arthur (in German) his family runs a gold mining business, and he was being held for ransom. Arthur doesn't understand what the man is saying. On returning to his family, the man gives Arthur a gold bar as a token of appreciation for rescuing him.
Later, the rest of the gang meet up with Arthur at their new campsite. Dutch likes the look of it and assures Arthur that they will make the best of it.

Get 5 headshots.

Assaults, kills, or abandons Charles;
Allows Charles to be killed;
Assaults or kills the family;
Assaults, kills, or abandons the hostage;
Kills or abandons their horse;
Dies.

title: Abe
text:
Abe is a minor character featured in Red Dead Redemption 2.
By 1907, Abe worked as a ranch head for David Geddes on Pronghorn Ranch, a relatively new ranch in West Elizabeth.
Events of Red Dead Redemption 2
In 1907, John Marston (under the pseudonym "Jim Milton") begins to work at Pronghorn under the guide of Abe and the ranch foreman Tom Dickens. During John's stay, Abe shows him around the ranch and assists him in milking cows.
At some point, the Laramie Gang and its leader decide to visit the ranch. The leader of the gang harasses and threatens Abe to convince his boss David Geddes into sell the ranch. John intervenes and tells gang leader to leave Abe alone. John provokes a fight with the gang leader and defeats the Laramie gang's leader. The gang leader states that he and his gang will return, before riding off the ranch. Abe then thanks Marston for his help.
Later that night, Abe helps Marston and Tom Dickens in repelling a Laramie gang attack, and the three are successful. When they arrive back at the ranch after an assault on the Laramie gang's hideout, John asks Abe to stay up just in case there is any more trouble, and to fire his rifle three times if he needs help.
Over the next few months, Abe continues working at the ranch. He is seen assisting John with various jobs on the ranch during the latter's time as a worker.
After John formally moves away from Pronghorn Ranch and purchases his own land at Beecher's Hope, Abe is not seen again; it is presumed that he continues working at Pronghorn Ranch as a hand.

title: Aberdeen Pig Farm
text:
Aberdeen Pig Farm is a ranch in Red Dead Redemption 2 and Red Dead Online in the Scarlett Meadows region of the Lemoyne territory.
It lies north of Pleasance and northeast of Lonnie's Shack, very close to the border with Roanoke Ridge, and is inhabited by siblings Bray and Tammy Aberdeen.
Aberdeen Pig Farm is a small ranch at the end of a dirt trail, beside the border with New Hanover. This pig farm consists of a large house, an outhouse, a small storage facility, an animal pen and a destroyed building, all surrounded by a wooden fence.
The largest structure in the farm is the sizeable wooden house. A small set of steps lead up to a roofed veranda that sits at the entrance of the home, equipped with a wooden railing, horse hitching post and other odds and ends. A lean-to stands at the southern side of the structure, housing a washroom and storage room.
Behind the front door is a large kitchen and dining room. A wooden dining table stands beside a stone fireplace, next to an open kitchen with wooden cabinets and shelves; two doors in the kitchen lead to the washroom and the back yard. In the next room is a parlor, equipped with a coach, desk, chairs and a sewing table. Between the kitchen and sitting room is a staircase that leads to the first story.
The landing upstairs features a chess table, fireplace, storage cabinet and an armoire containing a human skull and several other bones. To the left of the staircase is a door which leads to the master bedroom. This room is nicely decorated with wallpaper, carpet, a double bed and dressing table.
A few meters north of the house stands a wooden outhouse; continuing in the same direction, a storage shack sits a couple of yards away. Next to this storage facility is a fenced-off corral, and a few meters south of this is a destroyed structure. All that remains of this building is a decrepit wooden frame and thick growth of vegetation.
The property is littered with odds and ends, from a wagon to firewood and barrels to a clothing line. The grounds contain an abundance of vegetation, with trees strewn around the area, bushes surrounding the ranch and grass all over the property.
The Aberdeen Family may be based on the real-life Bender Family, nicknamed The Bloody Benders, who operated an Inn for unsuspecting travelers. They murdered at least eleven people, looted their corpses, and buried them in a mass grave while living in Kansas during the early 1870s. Like their counterparts in the game, John Bender Jr. and Kate Bender had an ambiguous and possibly incestuous relationship, with Kate reportedly being a free love advocate.
Coincidentally, one of the victims of The Bloody Benders was Abigail Roberts, murdered December 1872 and buried in the apple orchard on the property.
If the player returns to the homestead after retrieving their money, the house will be deserted. They cannot be encountered as Arthur after this.
Not too far from the farm is a shallow pit, where bodies are thrown into. This is where Bray and Tammy buried their mother after killing her.
If the player hogties Tammy and takes her to the burial site, she will apologize to her late mother.
The player can encounter a camper, who will tell them about the pig farm and the couple who live there. He tells the player that they offered him refreshments and dinner, but his feelings in gut told him not to trust them.
Interacting with the inhabitants while on the front porch enables players to access the room on the south side of the farm. Inside is a lockbox containing money.
Northwest of the farm and across the road, a dreamcatcher can be found.
Players can use the special encounter at Aberdeen Pig Farm for passing Arthur's money to John.
Just before the mission "Our Best Selves", go to the farm and allow Bray and Tammy to steal all of Arthur's money. After the mission "Motherhood" during Epilogue 1, revisit the farm as John and retrieve the money.
It is recommended for the player to kill Tammy and Bray as Arthur even if he intends to leave his money behind the portrait for John. If the siblings are left alive, John can still retrieve Arthur's money if the player left it untouched, but they will miss unique lines of dialogue and the opportunity to loot a lockbox and the rest of the house, as the farm will be long deserted by 1907.
According to the 2016 leaked map, the farm was originally located in The Heartlands region of New Hanover. This is included in a camper's dialogue, where they describe when they were riding through The Heartlands and came across the farm.
As such, while in the farm, the game will incorrectly display the player's bounty for New Hanover, instead of for Lemoyne.
